messages.text:
Good news on that one: the WS2000 sips power, so even at 20¢ it's cents a month, not dollars. It's $400 and earns WXM for reporting real weather from your address.

Where would you mount it, roof or yard?
Roof
Searched the catalog · WeatherXM WS2000 Helium Weather Station
Read the weatherxm helium weather station ws2000 page

Roof is the right spot — open sky, no shadows, and it's AA-battery powered (about 1.5 years a set), so your 12–20¢ never touches it. $400, in stock, ships in 2–5 business days.

One thing to check first: this WS2000 reports over Helium LoRa coverage, so you need a Helium hotspot nearby or your own. Do you have coverage where you are?
I have a bunch of old RAK Miners.  Can I use those?

Yes — if any of them is powered up and online on the Helium IoT network, the WS2000 will report through it. It doesn't have to be yours, but yours is ideal, and one live hotspot covers the station fine.

Which RAK model are they, and is one still running?
RAK7248

That one I won't guess on. The 7248 is the Pi-based DIY gateway, and whether it's still a valid Helium IoT gateway after the Solana migration depends on how it was onboarded — I don't want you buying a $400 station on my assumption.

I've put it to JD, who answers the hardware. He picks it up Monday at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.
Handed to the team · RAK7248 Helium IoT compatibility is outside the product facts; would not guess f

If you'd rather not wait on that: the WXM 4G-LTE WB3000 ($900) skips Helium coverage entirely and reports over cellular, so it works anywhere with a signal. Same roof mount, same rewards.

Want me to hold off until JD weighs in, or look at that one?
Let JD weigh in
Used the chat-interview skill

Sounds good — JD will have it Monday morning and the answer lands in your email.

Before you go, one thing: what made you look at a weather station rather than another miner?
I own a ski mountain and need a weather station

That changes the pick — a mountain usually wants more than one, at base and summit, and Helium coverage up high is unlikely, so the 4G-LTE WB3000 is probably the honest answer for the exposed spots.

That's a business install, so I've put it to Georges; he picks it up Monday at 10am ET and emails you.
Handed to the team · Business buyer, likely multi-unit install, needs a proper spec conversation.
How many spots on the mountain were you thinking of covering?
It's a little mountain

Then one at the summit may well do it, with the base lodge roof as a second later.

Last thing and I'll leave you alone: what's the data actually for — snowmaking calls, or posting conditions for skiers?
Snowmaking calls

That's useful to know — it means wet-bulb and reporting interval matter more than rewards do, and that's exactly what Georges should spec with you. He's got it along with the JD question, Monday 10am ET, by email.

Thanks for telling me, genuinely helpful.
